Moderately positive with cautious undertones. The FOMC notes strong job gains and a low unemployment rate alongside a moderate pace of activity; inflation is still below 2% but expected to move toward the target. The 25 bp hike, while keeping policy “accommodative,” aligns with New Keynesian insights that, with sticky prices and wages, gradualism in the policy rate helps limit real-side volatility (Christiano, Eichenbaum, and Evans 2005; Nakamura and Steinsson). The Committee’s emphasis on “symmetric” 2% inflation and close monitoring of inflation developments is consistent with inflation-targeting frameworks and the role of expectations in policy transmission (Svensson and Woodford 2005; Clarida, Galí, and Gertler). Market-based inflation compensation has risen but remains low, suggesting anchored expectations—an outcome associated with credible targeting. The use of interest on reserves and a corridor/channel system to maintain the funds rate target reflects modern operating procedures (Goodfriend 2002, ch. 11). Note that higher policy rates can raise near-term measured inflation via the cost channel (Ravenna and Walsh 2006), a mechanism related to the “price puzzle” in VARs, which justifies the Committee’s incremental approach. Net, conditions and literature support a modestly upbeat assessment tempered by signs of moderated household spending and business investment.
